title_en: Zhang Yiqian v. Management Office of Huaqing Pool, Lintong County — appeal of dispute over authorship attribution

full_text_en:
Zhang Yiqian v. Lintong County Huaqing Pool Management Office — appeal regarding dispute over authorship attribution

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Lintong County Huaqing Pool Management Office, Shaanxi Province

Legal Representative: Guan Zhizhong, Director of the Huaqing Pool Management Office

Agent ad litem: Guo Jianxun, lawyer of Lintong County Law Firm

Agent ad litem: Jiao Furen, lawyer of Weinan District Law Firm

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Zhang Yiqian, male, 52 years old, Associate Researcher of Shaanxi Provincial Art Research Institute

Agents ad litem: Li Zhenrong and Jing Binxue, lawyers of Xi'an Second Law Firm

Third Party: Shi Guolin, male, 50 years old, Art Editor of Guanghua Publishing House Xi'an Branch

Third Party: Wang Quan, male, 45 years old, Craft Artist of Shaanxi Huashan Bed Sheet Factory

Third Party: Shaanxi Provincial Art Research Institute

Legal Representative: Chen Xiaoying, Director of the Art Research Institute

Agent ad litem: Ye Tao, Researcher of the Art Research Institute

The appellant, Lintong County Huaqing Pool Management Office, Shaanxi Province, and the appellee, Zhang Yiqian, in the dispute over authorship attribution, dissatisfied with the civil judgment of Xi'an Intermediate People's Court, Shaanxi Province, dated June 4, 1988, filed an appeal to the Shaanxi High People's Court.

The Shaanxi High People's Court, in accordance with the second-instance procedure, lawfully formed a collegial panel and, upon trial, found the following facts:

On January 27, 1986, the Lintong County Huaqing Pool Management Office (hereinafter referred to as "the Huaqing Pool Management Office") and the Shaanxi Provincial Art Research Institute (hereinafter referred to as "the Provincial Art Research Institute") signed a mural creation agreement, and subsequently signed two supplementary agreements. The main contents of the agreement were: The Huaqing Pool Management Office commissioned the Provincial Art Research Institute to create a large mural titled "Yang Yuhuan Summoned to the Hot Spring Palace," and the Huaqing Pool Management Office would pay the Provincial Art Research Institute RMB 33,000. The completion time was six months, excluding the time for the Management Office to review the draft. After the agreement was signed, the Provincial Art Research Institute assigned its own painter, Zhang Yiqian, to create the mural. Zhang Yiqian spent eight months completing the mural creation, and with the assistance of Shi Guolin and Wang Quan, the draft was enlarged to a size of 9.15 meters by 3.6 meters. In mid-October 1986, the Huaqing Pool Management Office organized relevant department personnel and experts to review and approve the draft. After review, the Huaqing Pool Management Office decided to adopt it. In the process of sending the mural draft to the Chang'an County Marble Decoration Craft Art Factory for etching production, Zhang Yiqian, with the permission of the Provincial Art Research Institute but without consulting the Huaqing Pool Management Office, inscribed 19 characters on the right side of the mural: "Painted by Zhang Yiqian at Lishan in the Autumn of the Bingyin Year (1986), assisted by Shi Guolin and Wang Quan." Next to the inscription, there were also one personal seal and one official seal of Zhang Yiqian, and seals of Shi Guolin and Wang Quan. At the lower part of the mural, there was one title seal. In January 1987, the large mural "Yang Yuhuan Summoned to the Hot Spring Palace" was completed and installed at Huaqing Pool. Thereafter, the Huaqing Pool Management Office raised objections to the inscription on the mural and convened consultations with the Provincial Art Research Institute and Zhang Yiqian, but no consensus was reached. On September 10, 1987, the Huaqing Pool Management Office removed the inscription and the three seals from the mural, leaving only Zhang Yiqian's name seal and the title seal. Thereafter, the three parties consulted multiple times on the signature issue but failed to reach an agreement. Zhang Yiqian filed a lawsuit with the Xi'an Intermediate People's Court on the grounds that the Huaqing Pool Management Office had infringed his copyright. During the trial, after unsuccessful mediation, the court rendered the following judgment: (1) The Huaqing Pool Management Office shall, within 30 days after this judgment takes effect, restore the original inscription on "Yang Yuhuan Summoned to the Hot Spring Palace"; (2) The Huaqing Pool Management Office shall, after the judgment takes effect, offer an apology to Zhang Yiqian; (3) The Huaqing Pool Management Office shall, after the judgment takes effect, compensate Zhang Yiqian for moral damages in the amount of RMB 1,000. After the judgment was pronounced, the Huaqing Pool Management Office appealed, arguing that the mural was commissioned by the Management Office from the Provincial Art Research Institute according to the Management Office's requirements, and was not Zhang Yiqian's free creation. Zhang Yiqian countered that the right of attribution is the author's right and shall not be interfered with by others.

The Shaanxi High People's Court held that: the mural creation contract signed between the appellant, the Huaqing Pool Management Office, and the third party, the Provincial Art Research Institute, constituted a commissioning relationship, and the mural was a commissioned work. Therefore, both parties enjoyed the rights and assumed the corresponding obligations conferred by law. Zhang Yiqian, as the creator of the large mural, owned the copyright in accordance with Article 94 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC, and his right of attribution was protected by law. The Huaqing Pool Management Office, as the user of the mural, had the right to proper use within the agreed scope, which should be protected by law. However, it was improper for the Management Office to remove the author's inscription without authorization. Shi Guolin and Wang Quan were not the copyright owners of the mural. They only contributed labor in the process of enlarging the mural. Their labor should be recognized by society, but it did not constitute creation, and they had no right to be attributed as copyright owners. After the mural draft was approved by the Huaqing Pool Management Office, it became a work confirmed by both parties. The Huaqing Pool Management Office, the Provincial Art Research Institute, and the author Zhang Yiqian all had the responsibility to maintain the integrity of the work. The inappropriate actions of the three parties regarding the signature issue without mutual consultation were all in breach of the original agreement.

During the trial of this case in the Shaanxi High People's Court, the appellant and the appellee expressed apologies to each other, reached mutual understanding, and were willing to settle through mediation. On the basis of finding the facts and clarifying the responsibilities, the court, in accordance with Article 153 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC (for Trial Implementation), which provides that "the people's court of second instance may conduct mediation in hearing an appeal case," on July 31, 1989, through mediation, the parties voluntarily reached the following agreement:

1. Both parties express mutual understanding for their respective inappropriate actions regarding the inscription on the mural without prior consultation.

2. On the blank area of the right side of the mural, the inscription "Painted by Zhang Yiqian in the Autumn of the Bingyin Year" shall be re-inscribed, with a font size no smaller than 4×4 square centimeters.

3. The restoration work of the mural shall be undertaken by the Huaqing Pool Management Office and shall be completed within three months from the effective date of this mediation document.

4. In order to jointly maintain the overall artistic effect of the mural, Zhang Yiqian shall bear RMB 300 of the restoration costs, and the remaining costs shall be borne by the Huaqing Pool Management Office.

5. Zhang Yiqian's name seal at the upper right corner and the title seal at the lower left corner of the mural shall remain as they are.

6. Within three months from the effective date of this mediation document, the Huaqing Pool Management Office shall erect an explanatory stele at an appropriate location beside the mural. The inscription on the stele shall, in addition to recording relevant content, include the work done by the Shaanxi Provincial Art Research Institute, the author Zhang Yiqian, and Wang Quan and Shi Guolin.

The case acceptance fee of RMB 30 shall be borne equally by both parties, each paying RMB 15.
